Input explicitly supplies rational mu, positive-definite S_0 and independent Gaussian Fourier blocks (A_j,B_j) with covariance [[S_j,T_j],[-T_j,S_j]], symmetric S_j and skew T_j, j=1,...,d. X(t)=mu+Z_0+sum_j(A_j cos jt+B_j sin jt) is stationary on [0,2pi). A rational open full-dimensional polyhedron K={a_i^T x>b_i} has m facets; LP feasibility/redundancy checks are charged and empty-interior/full-space cases handled. Dense d counts toward complete input length L. For p=Pr{X enters K}, the source proposes relative-eps estimation with confidence 1-delta in poly(L,eps^-1,log delta^-1) bit operations without a multiplicative 1/p. Log p or a mantissa plus binary exponent is the output. Conditional trajectory samples have a coupling controlling uniform waveform error zeta except probability eta, with expected cost polynomial also in eta^-1 and log zeta^-1 and an explicit cutoff failure. Rational finite outputs are not literally total-variation close to a continuous law.

The witness W=1_{X(0) in K}+number of inward entries satisfies 1<=W<=K_*=md+1 on failure. Initial mass mu_0 and facet entry intensities mu_i sum to M=E W. The mixture Q of initial-conditioned and uniform-phase crossing-Palm laws satisfies dQ/dP=W/M, p=M E_Q(1/W), relative variance <=K_*-1 and O(K_* eps^-2 log delta^-1) proposals. Acceptance with probability 1/W gives conditional trajectories with acceptance >=1/K_*. An entry is not necessarily first; omitting initial mass breaks the event identity. For a face U=a_i^T X(0), V=a_i^T X'(0) and residual position Y conditional on U=b_i, mu_i=2pi phi_U(b_i) integral v_+ 1_other_facets g(Y,v)dYdv. Position-velocity correlations must be retained.

A height variable 0<=s<=v, v>=0 lifts each constrained flux to a Gaussian log-concave integral on a convex domain. Rational convex optimization finds q_*; write Z=exp(-q_*)J and compute in log form. The source supplies a normalized tail bound P(q-q_*>t)<=2^n exp(-t/2) and a bounded convex-body power lift with volume/2^k=integral(1-(q-q_*)/k)_+^k. With k of order t^2/eta, paid volume/sampling primitives, strict-feasibility slacks and inner/outer radii 2^+/-poly(L) are claimed to yield polynomial-bit acquisition. No supplied rare-event sampler or free warm start is assumed. This is a proof candidate with potentially large polynomial overhead; exact imported interfaces, rounding, radius, confidence and complexity proofs require independent audit.

Gaussian regression reconstructs all Fourier coefficients using c=c_0+Sigma H^T(H Sigma H^T)^-1(b-Hc_0), charging matrix work and induced correlations. Rational phase parametrization and tan(t/2) convert crossings to degree <=2d rational polynomials; Sturm root/sign isolation counts entries with the point at infinity and a planted root handled separately. There is no supplied minimum root separation. The source proposes proposal-normalized density and algebraic small-ball bounds to choose polynomial working precision, with proposal/count errors O(eps/K_*) because E_Q(1/W)>=1/K_*. Nonzero bad-polynomial, forced-degeneracy and full multivariate anti-concentration conditions remain important independent-review obligations. Reported cost is poly(L)+(m+1)I_conv+O(K_* eps^-2 log delta^-1)(S_conv+poly(D_c,m,d,b_work)); storage includes O((m+1)D_c^2) rational numbers and convex-body workspace. All convex preprocessing and output precision are charged.

This fits the acquisition-aware rare-event family near N492/N493 and the structured supplied-model probability algorithms N715/N719, while its stationary Gaussian/Palm mechanism warrants a separate card. It does not repair N493's relative-accuracy obstruction from small covariance error, solve N708/N721 hidden kinetic-channel acquisition, cover arbitrary nonstationary/infinite/singular/nonlinear models, give polylog cost in a binary maximum frequency, or provide global design optimization. Explicit unions cost their listed regions/facets; exponentially expanded Boolean geometry is not free. Covariance/data acquisition and infinite-spectrum truncation errors must be small relative to rare p. Rice/Palm, Gaussian excursion simulation, multiplicity correction, log-concave integration, minimax tilting and Sturm methods are credited antecedents. The recovered code/results concern only special-case diagnostics; general implementation, independent correctness, historical originality, practical advantage and technological readiness remain unresolved.
